name: Advanced Technology of Kentucky
old_description: Founded in 1990, Advanced Technology of Kentucky, also known as Advanced Technologies, and now as ATI MEDICAL SUPPLIES, has been working to provide patients with braces, mobility aids, cold therapy products, respiratory aids, and a number of other DME items to help them recover from a disease, recent injury or surgery.
about:
Advanced Technology of Kentucky, now operating as ATI Medical Supplies, was founded in 1990 in Florence, Kentucky. The company began as Advanced Technologies before adopting its current name, focusing on supplying durable medical equipment and clinical supplies to healthcare providers across the region.

The firm distributes a broad range of DME products including orthopedic bracing for neck, spine, shoulder, arm, wrist, hip, knee, foot, and ankle; cold therapy and continuous passive motion devices; bone stimulation and splinting systems; mobility aids such as crutches, walkers, canes, and bathroom safety equipment; lymphedema pumps and sleeves; respiratory devices including CPAP, nebulizers, and pulse oximeters; electrotherapy units for pain management; and hospital beds, wheelchairs, and incontinence supplies. In addition to product distribution, ATI operates an outside billing service that handles insurance claims for manufacturers and sales representatives bringing new products to market.

Customers include hospitals, surgery centers, urgent care clinics, orthopedic and primary care physician offices, home health agencies, rehabilitation centers, and college and high school athletic clinics throughout Ohio and Kentucky. The billing service extends to manufacturers and marketing teams nationwide seeking reimbursement support for DME products.

The company states its mission is to provide the highest quality medical supplies so healthcare providers can quickly treat patients and improve quality of life. It aims to simplify the insurance process, offering direct payment options when coverage is unavailable, and maintains contracts covering 99 percent of plans in Ohio and Kentucky including Medicare, Medicaid, commercial insurers, and workers' compensation, with additional Medicare and commercial contracts nationwide.
